chapters.title: b2
chapters.text: A ghost is an entity the server owns and mirrors to clients. Our capsule is one. So is the controller.

chapters.title: b4
chapters.text: Ghost Authoring Component on the prefab produces a serialization schema: which components, which fields, at what precision, with what change-detection. Baking generates serializer code per ghost type, no reflection at runtime.

chapters.title: b6
chapters.text: That third row is the whole design in one dropdown. Chapter 17 unpacks it.

chapters.title: b8
chapters.text: For a player capsule, Owner Predicted is nearly always right: you need your own capsule to respond in zero frames; you do not need someone else's to be frame-exact, you need it smooth.

chapters.title: b12
chapters.text: A snapshot is not the whole world. It is as much of it as fits in ~1200 bytes, prioritised. Low-importance ghosts update at a lower effective rate. This is a feature. Delta baselines are per connection. The server remembers what each client has ACKed. Loss is normal. The next snapshot re-bases automatically.

chapters.title: b13
chapters.text: Hardware analogy, importance scheduling is a weighted round-robin arbiter on a fixed-width bus. You do not get more bandwidth; you get to choose who wastes it.

chapters.title: b16
chapters.text: Fewer bits on the wire, and, crucially, quantized values compare equal more often, so delta compression finds more unchanged fields. Choose per field: position often 1000, rotation 1000, a health value maybe 1.

chapters.title: b17
chapters.text: Trap, quantization is a real precision loss, applied before the client compares predicted vs received. Set it too coarse and prediction will disagree with the server constantly, causing continuous micro-rollbacks that look like jitter. Set it too fine and you burn bandwidth. This is a tuning knob, not a formality.

chapters.title: b19
chapters.text: Ghost Relevancy lets the server decide a ghost simply does not exist for a given connection, interest management, fog of war, zoning. Nerve wraps this in a Relevancy Settings asset, which our project has registered on Server Settings.prefab.

chapters.title: b20
chapters.text: For two capsules on one map it does nothing. At 200 players it is the difference between shipping and not.

chapters.title: b22
chapters.text: Our capsules are server-spawned: Player Connection System instantiates on the server, and the client materialises them when the snapshot arrives. That is why ghosts=2 appears in the client world without the client ever calling Instantiate.

chapters.title: b23
chapters.text: Probe, see the schema Unity actually generated: `` Multiplayer then Ghost Snapshot Inspector (in play mode) `` It shows per-ghost byte cost. If a ghost is unexpectedly expensive, a field you did not mean to replicate is in the schema.
